hero.titleLine2: to Claude, Cursor, any MCP client
hero.lead: Give your AI agent a real SFR inbox. Read, search, send, reply, schedule and organize mail over IMAP with the SFR address and password you already use for the Webmail SFR.
hero.answer: Claude cannot reach an SFR mailbox on its own. MCPEmails is a hosted MCP server that connects it over IMAP at imap.sfr.fr on port 993, authenticating with your full sfr.fr address and your SFR password, so Claude, Cursor or any MCP client can read, search, send and organize the mail. SFR's own assistance page lists exactly these servers for every @sfr.fr, @neuf.fr, @cegetel.net and @9online.fr mailbox: imap.sfr.fr on 993 and smtp.sfr.fr on 465 with SSL/TLS, TLS 1.2 or 1.3, the complete address as the account name and your normal password. There is no app password to generate. One inbox is free, forever.

method.title: How SFR connects: IMAP on 993, SMTP on 465, one SFR password
method.body: SFR documents its servers on the assistance page about configuring a mail program. For sending, smtp.sfr.fr on port 465 with SSL/TLS or 587 with STARTTLS, using TLS 1.2 or 1.3; for receiving over IMAP, imap.sfr.fr on port 993 with TLS 1.2, 1.3 or SSL/TLS. Both hosts were confirmed from a live TLS connection and are shared by every SFR mailbox, so there is nothing regional or per-customer to look up. The account name is the complete address, and SFR's own example is prenom.nom@sfr.fr; the password is described simply as normal, the one you use for the Webmail SFR, which SFR says is already configured with your Espace Client identifiers. SFR adds a requirement worth noting: the Webmail no longer supports SSL and TLS 1.0 or 1.1, and it asks users of mail programs to move to TLS 1.2 or 1.3. MCPEmails connects with TLS 1.2 or later only, so that condition is met. One oddity on SFR's page: under the IMAP heading it pastes a Numericable example with @numericable.fr as the account name. For an SFR address the account name is the SFR address itself; the Numericable servers are a separate section for @numericable.fr and @noos.fr mailboxes.

setup.p: Sign up at mcpemails.com. The free plan connects one inbox forever and does not ask for a card.

setup.h: Check the address and password in the Webmail SFR first
setup.p: Sign in at webmail.sfr.fr with the full address you want to connect and your SFR password. SFR's own troubleshooting advice is the same: the identifier is your SFR email address, and a mail program that is refused should first be checked against the Webmail. If the Webmail refuses you too, reset the password from the Espace Client before going further.

setup.h: Mind the domain and the TLS version
setup.p: The same servers serve @sfr.fr, @neuf.fr, @cegetel.net, @club-internet.fr, @9online.fr and @9business.fr addresses. A @numericable.fr or @noos.fr mailbox uses imap.numericable.fr and smtps.numericable.fr instead, from the Numericable section of SFR's page. Whatever connects must speak TLS 1.2 or 1.3, which MCPEmails does.

Choose IMAP / SMTP, enter the full address such as prenom.nom@sfr.fr, and your SFR password. The SFR hosts and ports are prefilled and were verified from a live TLS connection. Then drop https://mcpemails.com/api/mcp into Claude, Cursor or ChatGPT, authorize, and your agent has the inbox.

gotchas.h: SFR blocks a mailbox after too many failed logins, and after six months unused
gotchas.p: SFR's access-problems page lists what gets an SFR mailbox blocked: too many unsuccessful connection attempts, too many emails sent in a short time, or sends from several IP addresses in a short time, and it adds that an address not used in the last six months may be blocked as well. A mail program retrying a wrong password is exactly the first case. SFR's remedy is to change the password and enter the new one on every device, browser and mail program. So get the password right in the Webmail before you let any client, MCPEmails included, try it repeatedly.

gotchas.h: No SASL-IR, so a client that assumes it gets a bare BAD
gotchas.p: SFR's IMAP banner is as short as they come (* OK IMAP4 ready) and it does not advertise SASL-IR. The server therefore rejects the one-step authentication that sends the credential along with the AUTHENTICATE command, replying with an unqualified BAD that is indistinguishable from bad credentials. MCPEmails detects the BAD and retries the two-step exchange, so this half is handled for you, but it is why other IMAP tooling fails against SFR with a message about the password.

gotchas.h: Sending is capped at 20 MB, which is low for a French ISP
gotchas.p: smtp.sfr.fr announces a maximum message size of 20,971,520 bytes. That is the encoded size of the whole message, and base64 inflates an attachment by roughly a third, so a file over about 15 MB on disk will not go. An agent asked to forward a large attachment gets a hard SMTP rejection at submission time rather than a slow send or a bounce later. SFR also suspends sending from a mailbox that sends too much too fast, so a bulk job should be paced.

gotchas.h: No IDLE, no MOVE and no SPECIAL-USE on a French-named mailbox
gotchas.p: The server advertises none of them. Without IDLE, new mail is discovered by polling rather than pushed on an open connection. Without MOVE, filing runs as a copy, a flag update and an expunge. Without SPECIAL-USE, Sent, Drafts and Trash are matched by name, and an SFR mailbox usually names them Envoyés, Brouillons and Corbeille. It does offer UIDPLUS, so at least a copied message reports its new UID back and does not have to be found by searching.

limits: The 20 MB submission cap is the practical ceiling on anything your agent sends from this mailbox.
Without IDLE, an instruction like tell me as soon as a reply lands is bounded by how often the mailbox is polled rather than by SFR's delivery speed.
Because the server has no MOVE support, a move is not atomic. If a connection drops mid-operation a message can briefly exist in both folders.

faq.q: Does Claude work with SFR Mail?
faq.a: Not on its own. Claude has no built-in SFR connector. Pointing an MCP server such as MCPEmails at the mailbox over IMAP gives Claude read, search, send, reply, schedule and organize access to it, and the same connection then works from Cursor, ChatGPT and other MCP clients.

faq.q: What are the SFR IMAP and SMTP settings?
faq.a: IMAP is imap.sfr.fr on port 993 with SSL/TLS. SMTP is smtp.sfr.fr on port 465 with SSL/TLS, or 587 with STARTTLS, with authentication required and TLS 1.2 or 1.3. The account name is your complete sfr.fr address and the password is your SFR password. Both hosts were confirmed from a live TLS connection and are the ones SFR's assistance page lists.

faq.q: Why is my SFR password rejected in a mail client?
faq.a: Check it in the Webmail SFR first, which is SFR's own advice: if it works there, the mail program has a typo, a wrong server or an old TLS version. If the Webmail refuses it too, the mailbox may be blocked after too many failed attempts or six months without use; change the password from the Espace Client and enter the new one everywhere. A VPN that changes your IP address often can also make SFR treat the attempts as suspicious.

faq.q: Does SFR issue an app password?
faq.a: No. SFR publishes no application-specific password for mail programs. Its page describes the password as normal: the same one you use for the Webmail SFR, with your complete address as the account name.

faq.q: Which SFR addresses use these servers?
faq.a: SFR lists @sfr.fr, @neuf.fr, @cegetel.net and @9online.fr for imap.sfr.fr and smtp.sfr.fr, and its troubleshooting page adds @club-internet.fr and @9business.fr as SFR addresses. Numericable and Noos mailboxes (@numericable.fr, @noos.fr and related domains) use imap.numericable.fr and smtps.numericable.fr on the same ports.

faq.q: Is my SFR mail stored on your servers?
faq.a: No. Messages are fetched live from SFR over IMAP for each request and handed to your AI client. Credentials are encrypted at rest and message bodies are not retained.
